# Issue #47: flag parsing treats "off " as true

A setting written as `off ` with a trailing space ends up enabled. This showed up
when reading feature switches from the environment. Please fix the flag parsing.

The bug is in `parse_flag`: it lowercases but never strips whitespace, so `"off "` doesn't match the false-words set. The docstring promises whitespace is ignored, and the empty check should also treat whitespace-only input as empty.

The sanity check confirmed the fix (the final `ValueError` is the expected behavior for whitespace-only input):

- `parse_flag('off ')` → `False` (previously `True` — the reported bug)
- `parse_flag(' OFF')` → `False`
- `parse_flag('on')` → `True`
- `parse_flags('on, off ,')` → `[True, False]`
- `parse_flag('  ')` → raises `ValueError("empty flag")`

All 3 tests pass.

arguments.summary: Fixed flag parsing in flags/parse.py: `parse_flag` now calls `text.strip().lower()` instead of just `text.lower()`, so values like "off " with trailing/leading whitespace are correctly recognized as false words instead of falling through to the default `True`. This also makes whitespace-only input raise `ValueError("empty flag")` as the docstring promises. Verified with the test suite (3/3 passing) and a manual sanity check of the issue's exact case.
